lawyer:
Farid Ahmed Advocate—For the Petitioners. 
ASM Abdur Razzaque with Nazmul Karim & Md Abdul Maleque Advocates—For Respondent Nos. 1 & 2.
parties:
Nilufer Hossain & others ----- Petitioners
vs
General Manager (Recovery), Uttara Bank Ltd and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
2. The salient facts relevant for disposal of the Rule, in short, are that respondent No. 2, Uttara Bank as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 351 of 1984 against Abul Hossain Talukder (now dead), the predecessor-in-interest of the petitioners for realisation of outstanding loan money in the court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka (respondent No. 3). On the other hand, said Abul Hossain Talukder as plaintiff filed a compensation suit being Money Suit No. 22 of 1985 before the same court against the respondent Nos. 1 and 2. After conclusion of trial, the Subordinate Judge, Dhaka by his judgment and decree dated 11-4-1999 decreed Title Suit No. 351 of 1984 in favour of the plaintiff Bank (Annexure-A) and dismissed the Money Suit No. 22 of 1985 on 26-4-1999 filed by Abul Hossain (Annexure A-1). 

 3. Thereafter the respondent No. 2, Uttara Bank filed Title Execution Case No. 9 of 2000 impleading the petitioners (heirs of the defendant) as judgment debtors (Annexure-B). The decree holder Bank on 25-6-2000 filed an application for encashing of the FDRs of the judgment debtors lying with the respondent No. 2, Uttara Bank and the court below allowed the said application and passed an order to adjust the same with the decretal amount. The petitioners came to know about the execution case through a daily newspaper and appeared before the respondent No. 3. On 18-9-2002 the petitioners filed an application under Order XXI, rule 90 of the Code of Civil Procedure (shortly, the Code) to set aside the auction sale stating that the judgment debtors were not parties of the original suit and after death of the sole defendant, Abul Hossain Talukder, the name of the present petitioners have not been substituted by filing an application within time under Order XXII, rule 4 of the Code and after hearing, the court rejected the said application on 18-9-2002. Being aggrieved by the order dated 25-6-2000 of encashing the FDRs, the judgment debtors petitioners moved this Court and obtained the present Rule. 

 4. Respondent Nos. 1 and 2 contested the Rule by filing an Affidavit-in-opposition denying the material averments made in the writ petition contending, inter alga, that the petitioners, legal heirs of the deceased Abul Hossain Talukder, informed neither the plaintiff Bank nor the trial Court about his death. So, the Bank could not take steps for substituting of this heirs in time in Title Suit No. 351 of 1984. However, when the matter came to the knowledge of the plaintiff Bank, the decree-holder Bank impleaded the legal heirs of the deceased Abul Hossain Talukder in the Execution Case No. 9 of 2000 and notices were duly served upon them. It is further stated that Mr Abul Hossain Talukder, the proprietor of Messrs Udayan Corporation, deposited some FDRs Issued in favour of Messrs Udayan Corporation as lien collateral security of loan with the decree-holder Bank which is also mentioned in both the plaint and judgment dated 19-4-1999 of Title Suit No. 351 of 1984 which was filed for realisation of the decretal amount with interest and cost of the suit by sale of mortgaged property. Mrs Nilufer Hossain (petitioner No. 1) also requested the decree holder Bank both in writing and verbally to encash the said FDRs for adjustment of liabilities of the Bank and therefore, there is no bar to encash the said FDR and adjust with the outstanding liabilities of the borrower before selling the mortgaged property. Accordingly, the Bank filed an application for permission to encash the said FDRs and court below lawfully allowed the same on 25-6-2000 and also allowed the amendment petition filed by the Bank after adjustment of the FDRs money with interest amounting to Taka 30,62,369 only with the outstanding liabilities on 13-9-2000 and the decretal amount was also corrected/amended in the Execution Form accordingly. Therefore, the impugned order, passed by the court below giving permission to encash the said FDRs is illegal. 

 5. Mr Farid Ahmed, the learned Advocate for the petitioners, submits that the respondent No. 2 Bank instituted Title Suit No. 351 of 1984 for realisation of loan money against the judgment debtor Abul Hossain Talukder, predecessor-in-interest of the petitioners wherein the 2(two) schedules of the immovable properties schedule "A and B" were given in the plaint for realisation of loan money with interest amounting Taka 1,53,24,890.24. In the schedule of the plaint the FDRs were not mentioned, but the court below, upon an application of the plaintiff Bank, passed an order to encash the FDR prior to sell the schedule property mentioned in the plaint and, as such, the impugned order is illegal and without lawful authority. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the petitioners are ready to pay the decretal amount to decree holder Bank by selling the mortgaged property and if after sale and the FDRs money any amount is left after adjustment of the decretal amount, the petitioners are entitled to get back the balance money with interest. 

 6. Mr ASM Abdur Razzaque, the learned Advocate for the respondent Nos. 1 and 2, submits that three FDRs were issued in favour of Messrs Udayan Corporation as pledge/lien collateral security of loan with the decree holder Bank. Some landed properties were also mortgaged in favour of the Bank which is stated in the schedule of the plaint. The learned Advocate further submits that the FDRs were pledged/lien as a security to the loan. So, in fact, no permission from the court was even required to encash the same Moreover, upon an application filed by the decreeholder Bank the court below passed the order for encashment of the FDRs money to adjust with decretal amount and no illegality was committed by the court below and, as such, the Rule is liable to be discharged. 

 8. Perused the writ petition, the affidavit-in-opposition, other materials on record and considered the submission of the learned Advocates for both the parties. It appears that judgment debtor took loan from the Bank on 29-10-1979 by mortgaging some landed properties and also pledged/lien the FDRs Subsequently Bank respondent No. 2 requested the defendant, predecessor-in-interest of the petitioners, to repay the loan money and finally issued notice on 16-2-1981 and the defendant, predecessors in interest of the petitioners failed to repay the same, the Bank respondent No. 2 as plaintiff filed the suit for realisation of Taka 1,53,24,890.24 which was decreed on 19-4-1999. Thereafter respondent Bank filed money execution case being. Title Execution Case No. 9 of 2000 on 9-5-2000. The decree holder Bank on 25-6-2000 filed an application to encash the FDR for partial adjustment of the decretal amount payable by the defendant judgment debtor, predecessor-in-interest of the petitioners to the decree holder Bank and the court below allowed the same. 

 10. It appears from the judgment of Title Suit No. 351 of 1984 and Money Suit No. 22 of 1985 that the defendant, predecessor-in-interest of the petitioners at the time of taking the loan mortgaged one tannery and landed property measuring 35 decimals and pledged/lien FDRs as security for repayment. The respondent Bank filed the suit for realisation of loan money with interest against the judgment debtor giving schedule 2(two) landed properties in the plaint and the court below passed the judgment and decree against the said schedule property (Schedule A) for realisation of money and the Bank encashed the FDRs to adjust with the decrtal amount with the permission of the court. 

 11. The petitioners did not deny the fact that the original defendant predecessor-in-interest of the petitioners took loan by pledging /lien the FDRs and deposited signed security document such as DP note, letter of authority to secure the repayment of the loan advanced to him in addition to mortgaging some landed properties. Since the FDRs and documents were signed by the defendant, predecessor-in-interest of the petitioners and letter of authority is there to repay the loan money, the plaintiff Bank has the right to adjust the loan money with interest by encashing the FDRs and selling the mortgaged property, if required. Thus, we are of the view that there is no illegality in the impugned order to encash the FDRs to adjust with the decreetal amount. 

 12. The respondent No. 2 Bank instituted the suit for realisation of Taka 1,53,24,890.24 with interest against the defendant predecessor-in-interest of the petitioners and it was decreed for the same amount. Subsequently, 3 FDRs were encashed by the Bank. So, after selling the decretal mortgaged property (schedule-A) the Bank would adjust the decretal amount and then should return the balance amount to the petitioners, if there is any. The executing court would look into the matter in accordance with law.
